# The Batch — stateful weekly saved-items feed

A phone-friendly static feed of your starred Gmail and X Bookmarks, refreshed every Saturday by a GitHub Actions cron. Items carry persistent state (`new|seen|sparred|acted|dismissed`) and spar/act threads that compound week over week.

## Gmail OAuth walkthrough

1. Google Cloud Console → new project → enable Gmail API.
2. OAuth consent screen → External → add your email as a test user.
3. Credentials → OAuth client ID → Desktop app → note Client ID + Secret.
4. OAuth 2.0 Playground → gear → "Use your own OAuth credentials" → paste ID+secret.
5. Authorize scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly` → allow → exchange for tokens → copy refresh token.
6. Repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → add GMAIL_CLIENT_ID, GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET, GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN.
7. Repo → Settings → Pages → deploy from main / root. Open the URL on your phone, add to home screen.

## Architecture

One **context store** (repo JSON) is the single source of truth. Two clients read/write it: a **phone-friendly static feed** (GitHub Pages) and **Dia on Mac** (via a write-back file). Item **state** and **spar/act threads** live in the store, never only in a client. Each Saturday the cron reads prior item state before writing the new batch, so the memory compounds week over week.

### File tree

```
batch/
├─ index.html
├─ updates.json                 # write-back channel; starts as []
├─ batches/
│   ├─ index.json
│   └─ 2026-08-01.json
├─ scripts/
│   ├─ gather-gmail.mjs
│   └─ lib.mjs
├─ .github/workflows/batch.yml
├─ package.json
└─ README.md
```

## Known limitation (by design, not a stopgap)

The static feed cannot write to the store server-side. Phone marks (seen/dismissed) and Dia spar/act updates are queued into `updates.json`, which the Saturday cron folds into the store on its next run. Write-back is therefore **asynchronous**.

The feed queues marks in `localStorage` and surfaces a **"Copy updates.json"** button so you can manually paste the pending marks into `updates.json` in the repo (or commit them via the GitHub UI) until the next cron fold.

When a persistent server-side store is added later, the write path becomes synchronous with no change to the store schema.

## Usage

```bash
npm install
# With secrets set:
node scripts/gather-gmail.mjs
# Without secrets (safe, exits 0):
node scripts/gather-gmail.mjs
```

The workflow runs every Saturday at 13:00 UTC and can be triggered manually via `workflow_dispatch`.

# Lineage App

[![CI](https://github.com/ortizjorge639/web-context-graph/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ortizjorge639/web-context-graph/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: AGPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL--3.0--or--later-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**Branch agent conversations into knowledge you own.**

Lineage App is a trusted, single-user, local-first agent conversation workspace. FastAPI serves the React interface on localhost, each GitHub Copilot CLI response becomes addressable Markdown blocks, and a branch can begin from any whole block while preserving its root-to-fork lineage and excluding sibling branches.

The interface is a view over a durable Knowledge Tree you own: `thread.md` stores conversation content, `meta.yaml` stores authoritative relationships, `index.md` is a regenerable discovery cache, and `AGENTS.md` explains the vault contract to other agent harnesses. Every mutation is committed to the vault's local Git history.

**Product landing:** [https://ortizjorge639.github.io/web-context-graph/](https://ortizjorge639.github.io/web-context-graph/)

> Lineage App is the product name. `web-context-graph` remains the repository slug and legacy technical name.

## Quickstart

Lineage App runs locally on Windows, macOS, and Linux. The UI runs in a modern browser; the host machine runs the backend and Copilot CLI.

### Prerequisites

- Git
- Python 3.11+
- Node.js 22+
- GitHub Copilot CLI with active Copilot access
- A modern browser

Clone the repository and authenticate the CLI once:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ortizjorge639/web-context-graph.git
cd web-context-graph
copilot login
```

Optionally choose a different vault directory, then start.

On macOS or Linux:

```bash
export WCG_VAULT_ROOT="$HOME/my-lineage-vault"
./scripts/run-local.sh
```

On Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:WCG_VAULT_ROOT = "$env:USERPROFILE\my-lineage-vault"
.\scripts\run-local.ps1
```

Without `WCG_VAULT_ROOT`, data lives in `~/web-context-graph-data/`. The launcher checks for Python, npm, Git, and `copilot`; creates the backend virtual environment if needed; installs project dependencies; builds the frontend; binds FastAPI to `127.0.0.1`; and opens the browser. It does not clone the repository, install system tools, provide Copilot access, or authenticate your account.

Set `PORT` to choose a different local port, or set `WCG_NO_OPEN=1` to start the server without opening a browser. Copilot CLI calls default to a 5-minute quiet-output timeout; set `WCG_COPILOT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` if your local agent regularly needs more time to respond.

## How it works

1. **Branch a block.** Each agent response is split into addressable Markdown blocks, with list items treated as separate branchable slices. Choose a whole block or item to begin the next request from that exact point.
2. **Preserve lineage.** The child thread receives root-to-fork context and continues independently; sibling branch content is excluded.
3. **Navigate the tree.** Map/Knowledge Tree views let you trace branches, return to a node, branch again, and open conversations.
4. **Own the artifact.** Plain Markdown and YAML remain useful outside the interface, while local Git records every mutation.

New root conversations open directly to the composer. The initial placeholder title is replaced from the first user request so you can start writing without naming the thread first.

Arbitrary highlighted-text or span branching is not implemented. Branching is block/list-item level today.

## Screenshots

Current captures from one coherent Lineage App journey:

**Linear thread** - begin with a normal Copilot conversation.

![A linear conversation in Lineage App](site/assets/product-thread-linear-desktop.webp)

**Branch from a block** - anchor a new prompt to one addressable response block.

![The branch composer anchored to a response block](site/assets/product-branch-from-chunk-desktop.webp)

**Isolated child context** - carry root-to-fork context into the child without sibling content.

![A child conversation with ancestor context above the current branch](site/assets/product-child-context-desktop.webp)

**Knowledge Tree** - trace branches, return to any node, and open its conversation.

![The Knowledge Tree connecting the conversation branches](site/assets/product-knowledge-tree-desktop.webp)

**Files and local vault** - inspect the durable Markdown, YAML, index, and folder hierarchy.

![The Files view showing the local Lineage App vault](site/assets/product-vault-files-desktop.webp)

## Promotional media

Watch the [17-second Lineage App highlight reel](media/promo/lineage-app-highlight-reel.mp4)
or inspect its [editable HyperFrames project](media/promo/lineage-app-highlight-reel/).

## Data, Git, and agent access

The vault defaults to `~/web-context-graph-data/` and can be changed with `WCG_VAULT_ROOT` when launching. It is separate from this source repository.

- `threads/<thread-id>/thread.md` contains Markdown role messages.
- `threads/<thread-id>/meta.yaml` is the structural source of truth.
- `index.md` is regenerated by scanning metadata and is never authoritative.
- `AGENTS.md` teaches external agent harnesses to discover threads, reconstruct root-to-current lineage, stop at recorded fork blocks, and exclude siblings.
- `graph-layout.json`, when present, stores presentation state only.

Existing `AGENTS.md` files are intentionally never overwritten. New vaults receive a guide that users can extend.

The Files view can reveal vault folders and files in the host file manager. It opens Finder on macOS, File Explorer on Windows, and the default file manager on Linux.

Lineage App initializes and commits to a local Git repository automatically. It does **not** configure or push to a GitHub remote. You may add and push your own remote manually; use a private repository when conversations may contain sensitive information.

## Provider and security boundaries

Lineage App invokes the installed and authenticated GitHub Copilot CLI directly as a subprocess with `--no-remote`. It does not use the Copilot SDK, has no arbitrary-provider adapter, and supports GitHub Copilot CLI only today. Available models come from your Copilot CLI account.

Do not expose the backend publicly. This is a trusted localhost app, and the current Copilot invocation has broad local tool access. The backend accepts only `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` Host headers (with any local port), rejecting non-local hosts before routing so a DNS-rebinding origin cannot become same-origin with the API. Browser JSON mutations are also limited to the documented local development origins by CORS, while no-Origin local CLI clients remain supported. A hosted multi-user service would require authentication, isolated workers, restricted tools, encrypted credentials, quotas, audit logging, and remote storage that do not exist here.

Copilot usage, subscriptions, model availability, and billing remain governed by GitHub.

## Manual development

Run the backend:

```bash
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/uvicorn main:app --reload
```

Run the frontend in a separate terminal:

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Test

```bash
# Backend fast suite (no real Copilot CLI calls)
cd backend
.venv/bin/pytest -v --ignore=test_smoke_e2e.py --ignore=test_copilot_engine.py

# Frontend
cd ../frontend
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
```

The full backend suite runs real authenticated Copilot CLI integration tests:

```bash
cd backend
.venv/bin/pytest -v
```

## FAQ

### What exactly is Lineage App?

A local-first browser workspace for branching GitHub Copilot CLI conversations at addressable response blocks and preserving the resulting lineage as a plain-file Knowledge Tree.

### Is it a desktop app or hosted service? What devices and platforms work today?

Neither. FastAPI serves a React web UI on localhost, and the host machine runs the backend and agent. The Bash launcher supports macOS and Linux-style environments. There is no supported native-Windows launcher and no hosted multi-user service.

### Which agents, models, and providers are supported?

GitHub Copilot CLI only. Lineage App invokes the installed CLI directly; it is not provider-neutral. Model availability follows the user's Copilot account and CLI.

### What do I need before starting?

Git, Python 3.11+, Node.js 22+, GitHub Copilot CLI with active access and authentication, and a modern browser on a macOS or Linux-style environment.

### Does the one-command launcher install everything?

No. After prerequisites, clone/download, and Copilot authentication are ready, `./scripts/run-local.sh` handles project dependencies, the production frontend build, localhost startup, and opening the browser.

### Where is my data, and how do I choose the directory?

The default is `~/web-context-graph-data/`. Set `WCG_VAULT_ROOT` before launching to use another directory.

### Does it sync to GitHub?

Not automatically. Each mutation is committed to local Git. You may configure and push a remote yourself; a private remote is recommended for sensitive conversations.

### Why not use NotebookLM or an LLM wiki?

NotebookLM is excellent for source-grounded synthesis, while LLM wikis can compile documents into useful pages and links. Lineage App solves a different problem: keeping you in control while knowledge is explored.

Every branch is a deliberate choice; its parent and fork point remain visible, sibling contexts stay isolated, and the complete tree remains inspectable as local Markdown, YAML, and Git history. It does not make AI infallible - it makes the path from question to answer auditable, revisable, and yours. The tools can complement one another.

### Can another agent harness consume the vault?

Yes. `AGENTS.md` documents discovery through `index.md`, authoritative relationships in `meta.yaml`, conversation content in `thread.md`, and the rule for reconstructing lineage without sibling leakage.

### Is it safe to expose publicly?

No. Keep it on trusted localhost. Copilot currently runs with broad local tool access.

### Is highlighted-text branching supported?

No. Responses are addressable at the Markdown block level. Arbitrary highlighted spans are future work.

### Is it free and open source?

The source is licensed under [GNU AGPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE). Copilot access, usage, subscription, and billing are governed separately by GitHub.

## Architecture and invariants

- `/edit` changes one thread in place and never cascades.
- `/refork` recursively deletes the selected child branch before creating its replacement.
- Creating a fork updates both child `forked_from` and parent `forked_children`.
- Rendering computes deterministic positional chunk IDs (`<thread-id>#c<order>`) from `thread.md` without rewriting stored Markdown.
- Backend mutations rebuild `index.md` and autocommit the external vault.
- Copilot session IDs are one-to-one with threads, and assembled context is root-to-current with siblings excluded.

See [`docs/plans/2026-08-27-web-context-graph-mvp.md`](docs/plans/2026-08-27-web-context-graph-mvp.md) for the legacy Web-Context Graph implementation decisions.

# Meeting Transcript Copilot for Microsoft Teams

This .NET 10 sample listens for Microsoft Teams meeting events, retrieves the meeting transcript from Microsoft Graph, and answers post-meeting questions with speaker- and timestamp-aware citations using Azure OpenAI and Microsoft Agent Framework.

> [!CAUTION]
> **Preview, not production-ready.** Transcript jobs and documents are JSON files on one App Service instance. The store has process-local locking and retention cleanup, but no distributed leases, transactions, encryption key isolation, legal hold, user deletion workflow, or multi-instance consistency. Keep App Service at one instance and use only non-sensitive test meetings until the production gaps are addressed.

## What is included

- Meeting start, end, join, and leave handlers.
- Asynchronous transcript polling with bounded retries.
- Tenant- and conversation-scoped transcript retrieval.
- Lexical context selection and cited transcript Q&A.
- Bounded model concurrency, queue wait, and answer timeout.
- Configurable local-file retention cleanup.
- Liveness, readiness, and build-version endpoints.
- An on-demand `diagnose transcript` meeting-chat command that reports whether
  Graph currently exposes transcript content without posting that content.
- An ACS Calling SDK browser participant that joins a scheduled Teams meeting,
  forwards finalized caption events, and makes the captured context queryable
  from that meeting's chat.
- Bicep and PowerShell for a repeatable new-tenant preview deployment.
- GitHub Actions validation and App Service deployment.
- Disabled-by-default rolling and meeting-to-date condensed summaries, with
  source-linked structured outcomes, restart checkpoints, and versioned private
  packaged instructions or optional private Blob instructions. Live summary acceptance and cloud activation are separate
  gates; follow the test runbook after an operator confirms deployment readiness.

## Architecture

1. Teams sends meeting activities to `/api/messages` through Azure Bot Service.
2. The meeting-end handler records a transcript job and returns immediately.
3. A hosted worker polls Microsoft Graph for the organizer's meeting transcript.
4. Parsed VTT cues become speaker-aware chunks stored under the configured data path.
5. The bot posts a readiness card in the meeting chat.
6. Questions in that chat select relevant chunks and invoke Azure OpenAI.
7. Responses are accepted only when they contain known source labels; deterministic speaker and timestamp notes are appended.

During an active meeting, the optional live-context POC follows a separate
source path: an admitted ACS browser participant receives finalized Teams
caption events, posts them to the App Service, and stores them under `/home`.
Questions in the active meeting chat prefer that meeting's captured live
context; completed Graph transcripts remain the fallback. After meeting end,
the same chat can use a read-only captured-caption snapshot until the completed
Graph transcript for that occurrence is available.

The current Graph call is app-only and uses `/users/{organizerId}/onlineMeetings/{meetingId}/transcripts`. It therefore requires organization-wide Graph application permissions **and** a Teams application access policy for each allowed organizer. Manifest RSC consent is not a substitute for that authorization path.

## 15-minute developer quickstart

### Prerequisites

- [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0)
- [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli)
- An Azure subscription where Azure OpenAI is available
- A Microsoft 365 tenant with Teams
- Roles needed for the selected steps:
  - Azure Contributor and User Access Administrator, or equivalent scoped roles
  - Application Administrator to create the app registration
  - Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator to grant Graph admin consent
  - Teams Administrator to configure transcript access and application access policy

### 1. Provision an isolated preview environment

Sign in to the intended Azure tenant and subscription, then run:

```powershell
az login --tenant <tenant-guid>
./infra/provision-tenant.ps1 `
  -NamePrefix meeting-copilot-dev `
  -ResourceGroup meeting-copilot-dev-rg `
  -Location centralus `
  -Subscription <subscription-id> `
  -LiveContextAccessKey <random-value-at-least-32-characters>
```

The script creates or reuses a single-tenant Entra app, configures the least-privileged `OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All` permission, creates a one-year bootstrap secret, and deploys App Service, Azure Bot with the Teams channel, Azure Communication Services, and a keyless Azure OpenAI account. It does **not** silently grant tenant admin consent unless `-GrantAdminConsent` is explicitly supplied by an authorized administrator. Store the live-context access key in an approved secret manager; it protects the POC token, meeting-resolution, and caption-ingestion endpoints.

On reruns, pass `-AppId <application-client-id>` to select the existing registration explicitly. Credential creation is additive so an unsuccessful deployment does not invalidate the previously deployed credential; remove superseded credentials only after the new deployment is validated.

### 2. Complete tenant administrator actions

1. In **Microsoft Entra admin center** > **App registrations** > the new app > **API permissions**, review and grant tenant-wide admin consent for:
   - `OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All` (Application)
2. Assign access only to test organizers:

```powershell
./infra/configure-teams-access.ps1 `
  -AppId <application-client-id> `
  -OrganizerIdentity organizer@contoso.com
```

1. In **Teams admin center**, confirm meeting transcription is allowed for the test users and that Graph transcript access and speaker attribution are enabled under the applicable meeting policies.
2. Wait up to 30 minutes for a new application access policy to affect Microsoft Graph.

See [Tenant and Teams administrator setup](docs/tenant-admin-setup.md) for the permission decision guide, policy details, and failure modes.

### 3. Publish the code

```powershell
Push-Location acs-calling-client
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
Pop-Location

dotnet restore --locked-mode
dotnet test tests/BotMeetings.Tests/BotMeetings.Tests.csproj -c Release --no-restore
dotnet publish BotMeetings.csproj -c Release --no-restore -o publish
```

Deploy the `publish` directory to the App Service created by Bicep. The supplied GitHub workflow does this for the repository's configured environment; update its environment variables and OIDC secrets before enabling it in another repository.

The checked-in workflow is pinned to the existing `meeting-poc-438871-izha3l56k5kdy` pilot in `bot-meeting-poc-rg`, subscription `cbab996c-0a31-4b66-bdcd-7ead3cad1487`, tenant `8caad56b-f716-4068-b468-3bdf8e4d357b`. It uses the protected `production` environment's existing `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, verifies the exact app/ACS resources and runtime configuration, and deploys application files only. It does not provision ACS, change permissions, or replace app settings or keys. Changing this target requires updating both the workflow and `infra/validate-pilot.ps1` deliberately.

Manual runs default to `validate_only=true`. A push whose commit message contains `[validate only]` also runs only the read-only preflight. Use that marker for a guarded merge, then dispatch `deploy-main.yml` on `main` with `validate_only=false` after the preflight succeeds. Deployment embeds the commit in the assembly and verifies it along with byte-for-byte ACS page/assets and endpoint health. Generated `.br`/`.gz` compression sidecars are not probed as standalone browser URLs. The health checks do not prove Graph/model access or live media behavior. No authenticated token probe creates an extra ACS identity during validation.

### 4. Build the Teams package

Use real, public HTTPS legal and support URLs owned by your organization:

```powershell
./infra/build-app-package.ps1 `
  -TeamsAppId <new-stable-teams-app-guid> `
  -BotAppId <application-client-id> `
  -WebAppUrl https://<app-name>.azurewebsites.net `
  -DeveloperName "Contoso" `
  -DeveloperWebsite https://contoso.com `
  -PrivacyUrl https://contoso.com/privacy `
  -TermsUrl https://contoso.com/terms
```

The package is written to `appPackage/build/bot-meetings.zip`. Keep both IDs stable when updating the app; changing the Teams app ID creates a different app.

### 5. Install and test

For development, in Teams select **Apps** > **Manage your apps** > **Upload an app** > **Upload a custom app**. Add it to a scheduled private meeting chat before the meeting starts.

If the global app picker omits a new meeting, use **Calendar > meeting > Chat with
participants > Chat dropdown > Add a tab > Meeting Copilot**. In the observed Teams
web flow, dismissing the app settings compatibility warning with **X** still added
the app. Confirm the chat's installation notice and the bot's meeting-start card;
installation alone does not establish an active meeting binding.

To test live context:

1. Inform participants before enabling or storing captions and follow applicable
   consent, retention, and privacy requirements. Start the scheduled meeting
   with at least one Teams participant and Meeting Copilot installed in its chat.
2. Open `https://<app-name>.azurewebsites.net/acs-participant/` in current
   Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome. Firefox captions are not supported.
3. Copy the **Join Meeting** link address from the bot's meeting-start card.
   Enter that link, participant display name, and configured live-context access
   key, then select **Join meeting**. Short `/meet/` invitation links and legacy
   `/l/meetup-join/` links are not interchangeable in the resolver. If there is no
   start card, stop and inspect the start event. Do not register an arbitrary link.
4. Admit the ACS participant from the Teams lobby unless the meeting permits it
   to bypass the lobby.
5. Confirm the page reports both ACS audio controls muted and captions active,
   then have at least two people speak. The page reports accepted, pending, and
   failed final captions separately. A successful POST needs an accepted receipt.
6. In the Teams meeting chat, type `@Meeting Copilot`, select the bot from the
   mention picker, and send a question whose answer was spoken after the ACS
   participant joined. The ACS participant (for example, "Live Context POC") only
   captures captions; mentioning it or speaking a question does not invoke Q&A.
   Verify that the bot's answer cites only captured live context. To check source
   availability first, send `@Meeting Copilot diagnose transcript` using a real
   bot mention.
7. Drain pending captions, leave ACS, and end the Teams meeting. In the same
   meeting chat, select an actual `@Meeting Copilot` mention and ask about a fresh
   fact again. Until a completed Graph transcript is available, expect
   a short note that the answer uses captured captions from the ended meeting,
   with speaker/timestamp citations. Use `diagnose transcript` for persistence
   time, age, and technical source details. Captured captions are not proof of
   Teams transcription.
   Ask an unstated fact too; the bot must not invent an answer.
8. Rejoin the same scheduled meeting for a later session and speak different
   synthetic facts. Verify that captions from earlier sessions are not used as
   current context, duplicate end events do not create duplicate jobs, and the
   later session can queue fresh Graph transcript work.

**Two roles, not two Q&A agents:** the ACS browser participant (default display
name **Live Context POC**) only captures captions. **Meeting Copilot** is the
installed Teams app bot that answers actual chat mentions. Speaking a question,
typing its name as plain text, or mentioning the ACS participant does not invoke
the app bot. Use the original meeting chat, not a separate personal bot chat.

#### Silent capture and clean proof

Teams and ACS are independent call legs. Muting Teams does not mute the browser's
microphone. The client joins with `audioOptions.muted = true` and calls
`muteIncomingAudio()` after connection, before starting captions. It monitors both
mute flags and stops the session if either confirmed mute state is lost. No
operator unmute control is exposed. Browser microphone permission is not a Teams
recording command, and SDK mute does not prove that the browser never opens a
microphone.

Initial mute flags are not treated as confirmed state while the call is connecting
or in the lobby. Captions remain stopped until the connected call confirms its
microphone mute and completes speaker mute. An unmuted connected microphone still
fails closed, as does losing either confirmed mute during capture or reconnection.

**Remaining live-test gate:** SDK 2.0.0 has no incoming-audio join option.
Post-connect speaker mute cannot rule out brief initial playback. Test join,
reconnect, denied microphone permission, and caption receipt with both audio paths
muted in a real Teams call. Do not claim a permission-free or zero-playback client
until those tests pass. Leave ACS to stop capture; use headphones or a separate
device for controlled diagnostics.

Use a new meeting with fresh non-sensitive facts. With Teams microphone on and
off, confirm ACS sends no speech. Test browser microphone permission allowed and
denied separately. Use two speakers on separate devices; one utterance must not
gain a second "Live Context POC" speaker. Partial then Final is normal progression:
only final events go to the server. The page shows the latest 50 final captions
by default. **Show raw events** exposes the latest 50 SDK events, including
partial revisions, for diagnostics only. Switching views never posts captions.
The recent final view suppresses an exact replay with the same speaker ID,
timestamp, and trimmed text; the server also deduplicates persisted finals.
Do not merge identical text across speakers
or remove a speaker by display name to hide an audio-source defect.

Caption delivery uses a memory-only queue of at most 100 pending events, a
10-second request timeout, a 60-second total age limit, and at most three retries
after the first attempt (1, 2, and 4 seconds). Network failures, timeouts, HTTP 408,
429, and 5xx retry; `Retry-After` is honored within the age bound. Other HTTP
failures stop the queue. Retries reuse the exact payload so server deduplication
remains effective. Queue overflow, expiry, and failed or abandoned delivery are
visible. Leave, refresh, crash, or closing the page can lose pending captions.
Drain the pending count before leaving. Call, agent, client, credential, listeners,
timers, and in-flight work are released on exit; page-exit cleanup is best effort.

The browser posts a client-reported status heartbeat every 15 seconds to the
key-protected `/api/live-context/status` endpoint. The server requires the active
meeting in the configured tenant, timestamps receipt, and marks status unknown
after 45 seconds without a heartbeat. Heartbeats are in-memory and reset on
server restart. They do not prove audio activity, successful caption persistence,
or a single capture client. A quiet meeting can have a current heartbeat and no
new captions. After disconnect, stored captions remain usable but are not proof
that capture continues.

Answers lead with the requested fact, followed by a short source-type note and
only the cited speakers/timestamps. Caption-based answers warn that coverage
may be incomplete; ended captions remain distinct from a meeting transcript.
Source notes show a single time for a caption instant, a range for a longer
chunk, and hours only when needed. Raw persistence/ingestion timestamps, age,
and capture diagnostics are reserved for `diagnose transcript`, not normal
answers, refusals, busy messages, or timeouts.

During a call, source selection prefers its captured captions and retains
the existing completed-transcript fallback when no captions are available.
After meeting end, it prefers a completed Graph transcript for that meeting
occurrence; otherwise it uses recent captions from the ended session. It does
not relabel old completed transcripts as current meeting context.

The server retains the latest ended-session binding for the same tenant and chat
under `EndedMeetings` in `active-meetings.json`, separate from active capture
bindings. It survives restart but never authorizes new captions, heartbeats, or
join-link resolution. `LiveContext__MaximumCaptionAgeHours` (24 by default)
bounds caption age and ended-binding availability. Starting another session
replaces that binding; only captions within the session's start/end window are
eligible. These are access limits, not automatic deletion of caption files.
Already-ended meetings whose bindings were removed by an older build cannot
be reconstructed automatically.

Graph ingestion deduplicates by tenant, meeting ID, and meeting-end timestamp.
A later session of a reused meeting gets a new job even if an earlier job was
Unavailable, Failed, or Completed. Existing legacy jobs remain readable and
duplicate end events remain idempotent. When the start timestamp is known,
Graph transcript metadata must fall within that session (using transcription
end time, or creation time if absent), preventing reuse of a historical artifact.

Mention Meeting Copilot and send `diagnose transcript` to check source context.
Capture heartbeat state is shown only for an active meeting, separately from
the Graph probe; an ended caption snapshot does not report capture as active.

The model context is not the browser's 50-row list. Each Q&A request selects
stored final-caption chunks (or completed-transcript chunks), up to
`TranscriptAgent__MaximumContextChunks` (50 by default). Partial recognition
updates never enter this context. Repeated final statements at different times,
and spoken corrections such as purple then green then blue, remain history.
Selection favors later chunks when relevance scores tie; model instructions
lead with the speaker's latest explicit update and its citation for a
current-value question. Superseded values appear only when the question asks
about history or changes; they are not discarded from the stored context.
The model must not invent agreement between different speakers.

Broad requests such as "what was the meeting about" select a bounded spread
across the session, including its start and end when the limit permits. A
topic-specific request with no matching material still receives a refusal.
This is bounded retrieval, not a guarantee that every stored statement fits
the model prompt; the token budget remains a separate production concern.

#### No-client assessment (November 5, 2026)

Read-only Work IQ path/schema discovery exposed
`/copilot/communications/realtimeActivityFeed/multiActivitySubscriptions` (create)
and `/{subscriptionId}` (fetch/delete). The create schema requires the caller's
own object ID, a meeting locator (join URL, numeric join ID/passcode, or organizer
metadata), and a transcript activity envelope. The resource schema returns
`activities.transcript.status` and `activities.transcript.transport.url`; its
description identifies a Work IQ SSE endpoint rather than a raw upstream WebSocket.
This identifies a concrete no-capture-browser candidate, not an implemented or
tenant-validated integration.

[Work IQ authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)
requires delegated user context (OBO supported; app-only unsupported) and uses
Copilot Credits. The existing app-only Graph transcript credential is not a
substitute. The connected developer MCP identity does not establish access for the
pilot app or tenant.

[Teams live-transcript rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-transcript-api-access)
require active transcription, AI allowed in the meeting, the correct delegated
permissions, and Work IQ enablement. The organizer's tenant controls access. The
separate Work IQ transcript access control takes effect November 14, 2026.
Unlike the observed ACS caption path, this route requires Teams transcription.

**Assessment: interface discovered; end-to-end proof blocked on approved access
and a controlled live meeting.** No subscription, auth flow, new scopes, billing,
consent, or tenant setting was created or changed. Before building an adapter,
confirm the pilot identity, exact delegated scopes, approved billing, stream
authentication/reconnect contract, meeting isolation, and fresh-fact retrieval.
A Teams tab still needs an open client and does not satisfy the no-client
constraint. Keep the existing architecture until a separate proof supports a change.

To test the existing Graph path:

1. Start transcription and have at least two people speak.
2. While the meeting is active, mention `@Meeting Copilot` using the picker and
   send `diagnose transcript` in the meeting chat.
   The bot makes one Graph list/content attempt and reports the observed status
   and content character count without posting transcript text.
3. End the meeting and wait for the readiness message.
4. Mention `@Meeting Copilot` in the same meeting chat and ask a question whose
   answer is explicit in the transcript.
5. Verify the answer, source label, speaker, timestamp, and tenant/chat isolation.

For organization-wide distribution, follow [Publish and validate in your organization](docs/publish-and-test.md).

## Local development

Create a git-ignored `appsettings.Development.json` and enter local secrets directly. Do not commit or paste its contents into logs:

```json
{
  "Teams": {
    "TenantId": "<tenant-guid>",
    "ClientId": "<application-client-id>",
    "ClientSecret": "<secret-value>"
  },
  "TranscriptAgent": {
    "Endpoint": "https://<account>.openai.azure.com/",
    "DeploymentName": "gpt-4.1-mini"
  },
  "LiveContext": {
    "Enabled": true,
    "AccessKey": "<random-value-at-least-32-characters>",
    "AcsConnectionString": "<acs-connection-string>",
    "DataPath": "App_Data/live-context"
  }
}
```

Authenticate to Azure for `DefaultAzureCredential`, then run `dotnet run`. Use a public HTTPS development tunnel and set the Azure Bot messaging endpoint to `<tunnel-url>/api/messages`.

## Configuration

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `Teams__TenantId` | required | Only this tenant is accepted. |
| `Teams__ClientId` | required | Entra application and Azure Bot app ID. |
| `Teams__ClientSecret` | required | Bot authentication secret. Store in Key Vault for production. |
| `TranscriptIngestion__DataPath` | local path | Use `/home/data/...` on single-instance App Service. |
| `TranscriptIngestion__MaximumWait` | 5 minutes | Maximum Graph publication polling window. |
| `TranscriptIngestion__MaximumAttempts` | 20 | Maximum ingestion attempts. |
| `TranscriptIngestion__RetentionPeriod` | 30 days | Deletes expired jobs and associated documents. |
| `TranscriptIngestion__PurgeInterval` | 6 hours | Cleanup frequency. |
| `TranscriptAgent__Endpoint` | required | Azure OpenAI endpoint. |
| `TranscriptAgent__DeploymentName` | `gpt-4.1-mini` | Model deployment name. |
| `TranscriptAgent__MaximumContextChunks` | 50 | Lexically ranked chunks sent to the model. |
| `TranscriptAgent__MaximumConcurrentAnswers` | 2 | In-process model concurrency. |
| `TranscriptAgent__QueueWaitTimeout` | 5 seconds | Admission wait before returning busy. |
| `TranscriptAgent__AnswerTimeout` | 2 minutes | Per-answer model deadline. |
| `LiveContext__Enabled` | `false` | Enables the protected ACS token, meeting-resolution, and caption-ingestion endpoints. |
| `LiveContext__AccessKey` | required when enabled | POC shared key of at least 32 characters. Never commit or log it. |
| `LiveContext__AcsConnectionString` | required when enabled | Server-only ACS credential used to issue short-lived VoIP tokens. |
| `LiveContext__DataPath` | `/home/data/...` | Meeting-isolated finalized-caption JSON storage. |
| `LiveContext__MaximumCaptionsPerMeeting` | 5000 | Per-meeting storage bound. |
| `LiveContext__MaximumCaptionAgeHours` | 24 | Bounds accepted/queryable caption age and ended-session binding availability; not file deletion. |

Runtime probes:

- `/health/live`: process is serving HTTP.
- `/health/ready`: startup configuration succeeded. This is not a dependency probe.
- `/version`: assembly version, embedded `BuildCommit` (or legacy `BUILD_COMMIT` setting), and `commitSource`. Automated deployment requires `commitSource=assembly`.

## Security and data handling

- Transcript text is treated as untrusted prompt data.
- Q&A lookup is scoped by tenant ID and Teams conversation ID.
- Live-caption writes are protected by a POC access key and resolved only
  against active meetings in the configured tenant. This shared key is not a
  production user-authorization model.
- ACS does not store captions. This application does, so participant notice,
  consent, retention, and deletion requirements apply before testing.
- Azure OpenAI local keys are disabled by Bicep; App Service uses managed identity.
- The Teams bot still uses a bootstrap client secret. Production deployments should use Key Vault references, rotation alerts, and a tested rotation runbook.
- Model citations are syntactically constrained to selected chunks; they are not claim-by-claim factual verification.
- `GlobalStandard` model deployments can process data outside the resource region. Choose an approved deployment type and region based on organizational residency requirements.
- Define notice, consent, retention, deletion, eDiscovery, legal hold, and acceptable-use policy with privacy/legal/compliance owners before real use.

See [Operations, privacy, and production readiness](docs/operations-and-production.md).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| `403 No application access policy found` | The organizer lacks the Teams application access policy, or propagation is incomplete. |
| `403 GraphAccessToTranscriptsDisabled` | Tenant Graph transcript access is disabled. |
| Transcript has no speakers | Speaker attribution is disabled by tenant policy or the returned format lacks attribution. |
| No transcript after meeting end | Transcription was not started, meeting type is unsupported, organizer policy is missing, or publication exceeded the polling window. |
| Bot does not receive events | Azure Bot endpoint/channel, app IDs, app installation scope, or manifest permissions are incorrect. |
| ACS participant remains in the lobby | A Teams participant must be present and admit it, unless meeting policy allows everyone to bypass the lobby. |
| ACS participant cannot join | Check the meeting link, external/anonymous meeting policy, ACS token endpoint, and browser diagnostics. |
| Captions do not start | Use current Edge or Chrome, confirm captions are allowed by Teams policy, and inspect the client diagnostics. Firefox is unsupported. |
| Caption delivery returns 404 | The bot did not capture the matching meeting-start event, or the pasted join link does not match the active meeting. |
| ACS participant does not answer | Expected: it only captures. In the original Teams meeting chat, select `@Meeting Copilot` from the mention picker and send the question. |
| Live Q&A has no context | Wait for an accepted final caption from the current session, then mention Meeting Copilot in that meeting chat. |
| Post-meeting Q&A has no context | Check that an ended binding and recent captions exist, or wait for the completed Graph transcript. An older build may already have removed the binding. |
| Reused meeting has an old Unavailable job | A later meeting-end timestamp queues a separate job; replaying the same end event does not. Teams transcription must still produce a new Graph artifact. |
| Q&A says no relevant material | No question terms or speaker names matched the transcript chunks. Ask a more specific question. |
| Q&A is busy or times out | Concurrency, queue-wait, or model timeout limits were reached. Check App Service and Azure OpenAI metrics. |

## Validation

```powershell

npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

# Meeting Transcript Copilot for Microsoft Teams

This .NET 10 sample listens for Microsoft Teams meeting events, retrieves the meeting transcript from Microsoft Graph, and answers post-meeting questions with speaker- and timestamp-aware citations using Azure OpenAI and Microsoft Agent Framework.

The store has process-local locking and retention cleanup, but no distributed leases, transactions, encryption key isolation, legal hold, user deletion workflow, or multi-instance consistency. Keep App Service at one instance and use only non-sensitive test meetings until the production gaps are addressed.

sections.title: What is included
sections.text:
## What is included

- Meeting start, end, join, and leave handlers.
- Asynchronous transcript polling with bounded retries.
- Tenant- and conversation-scoped transcript retrieval.
- Lexical context selection and cited transcript Q&A.
- Bounded model concurrency, queue wait, and answer timeout.
- Configurable local-file retention cleanup.
- Liveness, readiness, and build-version endpoints.
- An on-demand `diagnose transcript` meeting-chat command that reports whether
  Graph currently exposes transcript content without posting that content.
- An ACS Calling SDK browser participant that joins a scheduled Teams meeting,
  forwards finalized caption events, and makes the captured context queryable
  from that meeting's chat.
- Bicep and PowerShell for a repeatable new-tenant preview deployment.
- GitHub Actions validation and App Service deployment.
- Disabled-by-default rolling and meeting-to-date condensed summaries, with
  source-linked structured outcomes, restart checkpoints, and versioned private
  packaged instructions or optional private Blob instructions. Live summary acceptance and cloud activation are separate
  gates; follow the test runbook after an operator confirms deployment readiness.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.text:
## Architecture

1. Teams sends meeting activities to `/api/messages` through Azure Bot Service.
2. The meeting-end handler records a transcript job and returns immediately.
3. A hosted worker polls Microsoft Graph for the organizer's meeting transcript.
4. Parsed VTT cues become speaker-aware chunks stored under the configured data path.
5. The bot posts a readiness card in the meeting chat.
6. Questions in that chat select relevant chunks and invoke Azure OpenAI.
7. Responses are accepted only when they contain known source labels; deterministic speaker and timestamp notes are appended.

During an active meeting, the optional live-context POC follows a separate
source path: an admitted ACS browser participant receives finalized Teams
caption events, posts them to the App Service, and stores them under `/home`.
Questions in the active meeting chat prefer that meeting's captured live
context; completed Graph transcripts remain the fallback. After meeting end,
the same chat can use a read-only captured-caption snapshot until the completed
Graph transcript for that occurrence is available.

The current Graph call is app-only and uses `/users/{organizerId}/onlineMeetings/{meetingId}/transcripts`. It therefore requires organization-wide Graph application permissions **and** a Teams application access policy for each allowed organizer. Manifest RSC consent is not a substitute for that authorization path.

sections.title: 1. Provision an isolated preview environment
sections.text:
### 1. Provision an isolated preview environment

Sign in to the intended Azure tenant and subscription, then run:

```powershell
az login --tenant <tenant-guid>
./infra/provision-tenant.ps1 `
  -NamePrefix meeting-copilot-dev `
  -ResourceGroup meeting-copilot-dev-rg `
  -Location centralus `
  -Subscription <subscription-id> `
  -LiveContextAccessKey <random-value-at-least-32-characters>
```

The script creates or reuses a single-tenant Entra app, configures the least-privileged `OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All` permission, creates a one-year bootstrap secret, and deploys App Service, Azure Bot with the Teams channel, Azure Communication Services, and a keyless Azure OpenAI account. It does **not** silently grant tenant admin consent unless `-GrantAdminConsent` is explicitly supplied by an authorized administrator. Store the live-context access key in an approved secret manager; it protects the POC token, meeting-resolution, and caption-ingestion endpoints.

On reruns, pass `-AppId <application-client-id>` to select the existing registration explicitly. Credential creation is additive so an unsuccessful deployment does not invalidate the previously deployed credential; remove superseded credentials only after the new deployment is validated.

sections.text:
### 2. Complete tenant administrator actions

1. In **Microsoft Entra admin center** > **App registrations** > the new app > **API permissions**, review and grant tenant-wide admin consent for:

2. Assign access only to test organizers:

```powershell
./infra/configure-teams-access.ps1 `
  -AppId <application-client-id> `
  -OrganizerIdentity organizer@contoso.com
```

1. In **Teams admin center**, confirm meeting transcription is allowed for the test users and that Graph transcript access and speaker attribution are enabled under the applicable meeting policies.
2. Wait up to 30 minutes for a new application access policy to affect Microsoft Graph.

See [Tenant and Teams administrator setup](docs/tenant-admin-setup.md) for the permission decision guide, policy details, and failure modes.

sections.title: 3. Publish the code
sections.text:
### 3. Publish the code

```powershell
Push-Location acs-calling-client
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
Pop-Location

dotnet restore --locked-mode
dotnet test tests/BotMeetings.Tests/BotMeetings.Tests.csproj -c Release --no-restore
dotnet publish BotMeetings.csproj -c Release --no-restore -o publish
```

Deploy the `publish` directory to the App Service created by Bicep. The supplied GitHub workflow does this for the repository's configured environment; update its environment variables and OIDC secrets before enabling it in another repository.

The checked-in workflow is pinned to the existing `meeting-poc-438871-izha3l56k5kdy` pilot in `bot-meeting-poc-rg`, subscription `cbab996c-0a31-4b66-bdcd-7ead3cad1487`, tenant `8caad56b-f716-4068-b468-3bdf8e4d357b`. It uses the protected `production` environment's existing `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, verifies the exact app/ACS resources and runtime configuration, and deploys application files only. It does not provision ACS, change permissions, or replace app settings or keys. Changing this target requires updating both the workflow and `infra/validate-pilot.ps1` deliberately.

Manual runs default to `validate_only=true`. A push whose commit message contains `[validate only]` also runs only the read-only preflight. Use that marker for a guarded merge, then dispatch `deploy-main.yml` on `main` with `validate_only=false` after the preflight succeeds. Deployment embeds the commit in the assembly and verifies it along with byte-for-byte ACS page/assets and endpoint health. Generated `.br`/`.gz` compression sidecars are not probed as standalone browser URLs. The health checks do not prove Graph/model access or live media behavior. No authenticated token probe creates an extra ACS identity during validation.

sections.text:
### 5. Install and test

For development, in Teams select **Apps** > **Manage your apps** > **Upload an app** > **Upload a custom app**. Add it to a scheduled private meeting chat before the meeting starts.

If the global app picker omits a new meeting, use **Calendar > meeting > Chat with
participants > Chat dropdown > Add a tab > Meeting Copilot**. In the observed Teams
web flow, dismissing the app settings compatibility warning with **X** still added
the app. Confirm the chat's installation notice and the bot's meeting-start card;
installation alone does not establish an active meeting binding.

To test live context:

1. Inform participants before enabling or storing captions and follow applicable
   consent, retention, and privacy requirements. Start the scheduled meeting
   with at least one Teams participant and Meeting Copilot installed in its chat.
2. Open `https://<app-name>.azurewebsites.net/acs-participant/` in current
   Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome. Firefox captions are not supported.
3. Copy the **Join Meeting** link address from the bot's meeting-start card.
   Enter that link, participant display name, and configured live-context access
   key, then select **Join meeting**. Short `/meet/` invitation links and legacy
   `/l/meetup-join/` links are not interchangeable in the resolver. If there is no
   start card, stop and inspect the start event. Do not register an arbitrary link.
4. Admit the ACS participant from the Teams lobby unless the meeting permits it
   to bypass the lobby.
5. Confirm the page reports both ACS audio controls muted and captions active,
   then have at least two people speak. The page reports accepted, pending, and
   failed final captions separately. A successful POST needs an accepted receipt.
6. In the Teams meeting chat, type `@Meeting Copilot`, select the bot from the
   mention picker, and send a question whose answer was spoken after the ACS
   participant joined. The ACS participant (for example, "Live Context POC") only
   captures captions; mentioning it or speaking a question does not invoke Q&A.
   Verify that the bot's answer cites only captured live context. To check source
   availability first, send `@Mee

sections.title: 5. Install and test
sections.text:
ting Copilot diagnose transcript` using a real
   bot mention.
7. Drain pending captions, leave ACS, and end the Teams meeting. In the same
   meeting chat, select an actual `@Meeting Copilot` mention and ask about a fresh
   fact again. Until a completed Graph transcript is available, expect
   a short note that the answer uses captured captions from the ended meeting,
   with speaker/timestamp citations. Use `diagnose transcript` for persistence
   time, age, and technical source details. Captured captions are not proof of
   Teams transcription.
   Ask an unstated fact too; the bot must not invent an answer.
8. Rejoin the same scheduled meeting for a later session and speak different
   synthetic facts. Verify that captions from earlier sessions are not used as
   current context, duplicate end events do not create duplicate jobs, and the
   later session can queue fresh Graph transcript work.

**Two roles, not two Q&A agents:** the ACS browser participant (default display
name **Live Context POC**) only captures captions. **Meeting Copilot** is the
installed Teams app bot that answers actual chat mentions. Speaking a question,
typing its name as plain text, or mentioning the ACS participant does not invoke
the app bot. Use the original meeting chat, not a separate personal bot chat.

sections.title: Silent capture and clean proof
sections.text:
#### Silent capture and clean proof

Teams and ACS are independent call legs. Muting Teams does not mute the browser's
microphone. The client joins with `audioOptions.muted = true` and calls
`muteIncomingAudio()` after connection, before starting captions. It monitors both
mute flags and stops the session if either confirmed mute state is lost. No
operator unmute control is exposed. Browser microphone permission is not a Teams
recording command, and SDK mute does not prove that the browser never opens a
microphone.

Initial mute flags are not treated as confirmed state while the call is connecting
or in the lobby. Captions remain stopped until the connected call confirms its
microphone mute and completes speaker mute. An unmuted connected microphone still
fails closed, as does losing either confirmed mute during capture or reconnection.

**Remaining live-test gate:** SDK 2.0.0 has no incoming-audio join option.
Post-connect speaker mute cannot rule out brief initial playback. Test join,
reconnect, denied microphone permission, and caption receipt with both audio paths
muted in a real Teams call. Do not claim a permission-free or zero-playback client
until those tests pass. Leave ACS to stop capture; use headphones or a separate
device for controlled diagnostics.

Use a new meeting with fresh non-sensitive facts. With Teams microphone on and
off, confirm ACS sends no speech. Test browser microphone permission allowed and
denied separately. Use two speakers on separate devices; one utterance must not
gain a second "Live Context POC" speaker. Partial then Final is normal progression:
only final events go to the server. The page shows the latest 50 final captions
by default. **Show raw events** exposes the latest 50 SDK events, including
partial revisions, for diagnostics only. Switching views never posts captions.
The recent final view suppresses an exact replay with the same speaker ID,
timestamp, and trimmed text; the server also deduplicates persisted finals.
Do not merge identical text across speakers
or remove a speaker by display name to hide an audio-source defect.

Caption delivery uses a memory-only queue of at most 100 pending events, a
10-second request

sections.title: Silent capture and clean proof
sections.text:
timeout, a 60-second total age limit, and at most three retries
after the first attempt (1, 2, and 4 seconds). Network failures, timeouts, HTTP 408,
429, and 5xx retry; `Retry-After` is honored within the age bound. Other HTTP
failures stop the queue. Retries reuse the exact payload so server deduplication
remains effective. Queue overflow, expiry, and failed or abandoned delivery are
visible. Leave, refresh, crash, or closing the page can lose pending captions.
Drain the pending count before leaving. Call, agent, client, credential, listeners,
timers, and in-flight work are released on exit; page-exit cleanup is best effort.

The browser posts a client-reported status heartbeat every 15 seconds to the
key-protected `/api/live-context/status` endpoint. The server requires the active
meeting in the configured tenant, timestamps receipt, and marks status unknown
after 45 seconds without a heartbeat. Heartbeats are in-memory and reset on
server restart. They do not prove audio activity, successful caption persistence,
or a single capture client. A quiet meeting can have a current heartbeat and no
new captions. After disconnect, stored captions remain usable but are not proof
that capture continues.

Answers lead with the requested fact, followed by a short source-type note and
only the cited speakers/timestamps. Caption-based answers warn that coverage
may be incomplete; ended captions remain distinct from a meeting transcript.
Source notes show a single time for a caption instant, a range for a longer
chunk, and hours only when needed. Raw persistence/ingestion timestamps, age,
and capture diagnostics are reserved for `diagnose transcript`, not normal
answers, refusals, busy messages, or timeouts.

During a call, source selection prefers its captured captions and retains
the existing completed-transcript fallback when no captions are available.
After meeting end, it prefers a completed Graph transcript for that meeting
occurrence; otherwise it uses recent captions from the ended session. It does
not relabel old completed transcripts as current meeting context.

The server retains the latest ended-session binding for the same tenant and chat
under `EndedMeetings` i

sections.title: Silent capture and clean proof
sections.text:
n `active-meetings.json`, separate from active capture
bindings. It survives restart but never authorizes new captions, heartbeats, or
join-link resolution. `LiveContext__MaximumCaptionAgeHours` (24 by default)
bounds caption age and ended-binding availability. Starting another session
replaces that binding; only captions within the session's start/end window are
eligible. These are access limits, not automatic deletion of caption files.
Already-ended meetings whose bindings were removed by an older build cannot
be reconstructed automatically.

Graph ingestion deduplicates by tenant, meeting ID, and meeting-end timestamp.
A later session of a reused meeting gets a new job even if an earlier job was
Unavailable, Failed, or Completed. Existing legacy jobs remain readable and
duplicate end events remain idempotent. When the start timestamp is known,
Graph transcript metadata must fall within that session (using transcription
end time, or creation time if absent), preventing reuse of a historical artifact.

Mention Meeting Copilot and send `diagnose transcript` to check source context.
Capture heartbeat state is shown only for an active meeting, separately from
the Graph probe; an ended caption snapshot does not report capture as active.

The model context is not the browser's 50-row list. Each Q&A request selects
stored final-caption chunks (or completed-transcript chunks), up to
`TranscriptAgent__MaximumContextChunks` (50 by default). Partial recognition
updates never enter this context. Repeated final statements at different times,
and spoken corrections such as purple then green then blue, remain history.
Selection favors later chunks when relevance scores tie; model instructions
lead with the speaker's latest explicit update and its citation for a
current-value question. Superseded values appear only when the question asks
about history or changes; they are not discarded from the stored context.
The model must not invent agreement between different speakers.

Broad requests such as "what was the meeting about" select a bounded spread
across the session, including its start and end when the limit permits. A
topic-specific request with no matching material still

sections.title: Silent capture and clean proof
sections.text:
receives a refusal.
This is bounded retrieval, not a guarantee that every stored statement fits
the model prompt; the token budget remains a separate production concern.

sections.title: No-client assessment (November 5, 2026)
sections.text:
#### No-client assessment (November 5, 2026)

Read-only Work IQ path/schema discovery exposed
`/copilot/communications/realtimeActivityFeed/multiActivitySubscriptions` (create)
and `/{subscriptionId}` (fetch/delete). The create schema requires the caller's
own object ID, a meeting locator (join URL, numeric join ID/passcode, or organizer
metadata), and a transcript activity envelope. The resource schema returns
`activities.transcript.status` and `activities.transcript.transport.url`; its
description identifies a Work IQ SSE endpoint rather than a raw upstream WebSocket.
This identifies a concrete no-capture-browser candidate, not an implemented or
tenant-validated integration.

[Work IQ authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)
requires delegated user context (OBO supported; app-only unsupported) and uses
Copilot Credits. The existing app-only Graph transcript credential is not a
substitute. The connected developer MCP identity does not establish access for the
pilot app or tenant.

[Teams live-transcript rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-transcript-api-access)
require active transcription, AI allowed in the meeting, the correct delegated
permissions, and Work IQ enablement. The organizer's tenant controls access. The
separate Work IQ transcript access control takes effect November 14, 2026.
Unlike the observed ACS caption path, this route requires Teams transcription.

**Assessment: interface discovered; end-to-end proof blocked on approved access
and a controlled live meeting.** No subscription, auth flow, new scopes, billing,
consent, or tenant setting was created or changed. Before building an adapter,
confirm the pilot identity, exact delegated scopes, approved billing, stream
authentication/reconnect contract, meeting isolation, and fresh-fact retrieval.
A Teams tab still needs an open client and does not satisfy the no-client
constraint. Keep the existing architecture until a separate proof supports a change.

To test the existing Graph path:

1. Start transcription and have at least two people speak.
2. While the meeting is active, mention `@Meeting Copilot` u

sections.title: No-client assessment (November 5, 2026)
sections.text:
sing the picker and
   send `diagnose transcript` in the meeting chat.
   The bot makes one Graph list/content attempt and reports the observed status
   and content character count without posting transcript text.
3. End the meeting and wait for the readiness message.
4. Mention `@Meeting Copilot` in the same meeting chat and ask a question whose
   answer is explicit in the transcript.
5. Verify the answer, source label, speaker, timestamp, and tenant/chat isolation.

For organization-wide distribution, follow [Publish and validate in your organization](docs/publish-and-test.md).

sections.title: Security and data handling
sections.text:
## Security and data handling

- Transcript text is treated as untrusted prompt data.
- Q&A lookup is scoped by tenant ID and Teams conversation ID.
- Live-caption writes are protected by a POC access key and resolved only
  against active meetings in the configured tenant. This shared key is not a
  production user-authorization model.
- ACS does not store captions. This application does, so participant notice,
  consent, retention, and deletion requirements apply before testing.
- Azure OpenAI local keys are disabled by Bicep; App Service uses managed identity.
- The Teams bot still uses a bootstrap client secret. Production deployments should use Key Vault references, rotation alerts, and a tested rotation runbook.
- Model citations are syntactically constrained to selected chunks; they are not claim-by-claim factual verification.
- `GlobalStandard` model deployments can process data outside the resource region. Choose an approved deployment type and region based on organizational residency requirements.
- Define notice, consent, retention, deletion, eDiscovery, legal hold, and acceptable-use policy with privacy/legal/compliance owners before real use.

See [Operations, privacy, and production readiness](docs/operations-and-production.md).

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| `403 No application access policy found` | The organizer lacks the Teams application access policy, or propagation is incomplete. |
| `403 GraphAccessToTranscriptsDisabled` | Tenant Graph transcript access is disabled. |
| Transcript has no speakers | Speaker attribution is disabled by tenant policy or the returned format lacks attribution. |
| No transcript after meeting end | Transcription was not started, meeting type is unsupported, organizer policy is missing, or publication exceeded the polling window. |
| Bot does not receive events | Azure Bot endpoint/channel, app IDs, app installation scope, or manifest permissions are incorrect. |
| ACS participant remains in the lobby | A Teams participant must be present and admit it, unless meeting policy allows everyone to bypass the lobby. |
| ACS participant cannot join | Check the meeting link, external/anonymous meeting policy, ACS token endpoint, and browser diagnostics. |
| Captions do not start | Use current Edge or Chrome, confirm captions are allowed by Teams policy, and inspect the client diagnostics. Firefox is unsupported. |
| Caption delivery returns 404 | The bot did not capture the matching meeting-start event, or the pasted join link does not match the active meeting. |
| ACS participant does not answer | Expected: it only captures. In the original Teams meeting chat, select `@Meeting Copilot` from the mention picker and send the question. |
| Live Q&A has no context | Wait for an accepted final caption from the current session, then mention Meeting Copilot in that meeting chat. |
| Post-meeting Q&A has no context | Check that an ended binding and recent captions exist, or wait for the completed Graph transcript. An older build may already have removed the binding. |
| Reused meeting has an old Unavailable job | A later meeting-end timestamp queues a separate job; replaying the same end event does not. Teams transcription must still produce a new Graph artifact. |
| Q&A says no relevant material | No question terms or speaker names matched the transcript chunks. Ask a more specific question. |
| Q&A is busy or times out | Concurrency, q

# MCreator Workspace Harness

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

An agent skill and field guide for safely connecting coding agents to local
[MCreator](https://mcreator.net/) workspaces.

It teaches agents how to create and modify procedures, coordinate Blockly
definitions with generated Java, survive MCreator regeneration, compile with
the bundled JDK, and prove behavior inside Minecraft through real-time logs.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Close MCreator before an agent writes workspace files. MCreator can overwrite
> external changes from its in-memory workspace model.

## Why this exists

Complex MCreator work spans several representations:

- The workspace index (`.mcreator`)
- Mod element definitions (`elements/*.mod.json`)
- Embedded Blockly XML
- Generated Java
- Hooking elements such as tools or blocks
- The running Minecraft client and integrated server

Changing only one layer can compile yet still disappear from MCreator, be
regenerated away, or never execute in Minecraft. This harness treats the whole
path as one testable system.

## What agents learn

- Discover and inspect an MCreator workspace safely.
- Add a procedure that appears in MCreator's block editor.
- Wire procedures to item, block, or entity triggers.
- Read installed MCreator block schemas and generator templates.
- Choose between block-editable and code-locked workflows.
- Use server-authoritative item state for reliable counters.
- Compile with the workspace Gradle wrapper and MCreator JDK.
- Tail `run/logs/latest.log` while a user tests in Minecraft.
- Distinguish visual sameness from registry-level state.
- Recover when an open MCreator session overwrites external edits.

## Install as a Copilot CLI skill

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/ortizjorge639/mcreator-workspace-harness.git `
  "$HOME\.copilot\skills\mcreator-workspace-harness"
```

Restart Copilot CLI, then open `/skills`. The skill activates for requests
about direct MCreator workspace automation, procedures, generated Java, or
Run Client tracing.

For another agent that supports the open Agent Skills convention, clone the
repository into its skills directory, such as:

```text
~/.agents/skills/mcreator-workspace-harness
```

## Quick start for users

1. Back up or commit your MCreator workspace.
2. Tell the agent the workspace name and desired behavior.
3. Close MCreator before the agent edits.
4. Let the agent inspect all related elements before writing.
5. Reopen MCreator only after JSON/XML validation and compilation.
